hero.heading: What this component does
hero.description: A row in the Navigation Rail's sub menu panel, with a leading glyph, a label, an optional badge and an optional caret. It is the content the rail's Sub Menu Slot is built around, placed either directly or inside a Collapsible Menu Item. Nesting is a property rather than a layout, indenting the row and quietening its label so one level of hierarchy reads without connector lines.

rows.Description: The resting row.
Documents the pointer-over treatment. The implementation drives this, so choosing it in a layout freezes the row in a state it should not be in.
Documents the pointer-down treatment. It also shifts the label token, which hover does not.
The row the user is currently on. It is the only state with a background of its own rather than a borrowed scrim, and it recolours the label as well.
The row can be selected.
The row is unavailable, and nothing on it explains why. Offered on the resting state only, so a row cannot be shown selected and disabled at once.
A first-level row in the panel.

A child row under a collapsible parent. It indents from the leading edge and steps the label down to a quieter token and a smaller type style, so depth reads without a connector line. Only one level of nesting is built.
The row's name. The row is a fixed width and the text does not truncate or wrap, so a long name overflows rather than shortening.
Shows a glyph before the label, which is what keeps rows scannable in a long list.
Hides it. The label shifts to the leading edge, so a list mixing rows with and without icons loses its alignment.
Shows the caret at the trailing edge, marking the row as one that opens a further level.
Hides the caret, for a row that navigates straight to its destination. Leaving it on for a row that opens nothing promises a level that is not there.
No badge on the row.
Reveals a notification indicator between the label and the trailing caret. Unlike the rail item's badge this one sits in the layout, so it takes space from the label.

rows.What changes: No background at all. The label sits on foreground/primary, or foreground/secondary when nested.
A ghost scrim at 5 percent opacity appears behind the row. The label does not change.
The ghost scrim at 10 percent, and the label moves to interactive/neutral/foreground/default. This is the one state where nested and unnested rows converge on the same label token.
A background on interactive/ghost/background/selected at 5 percent, the only state with a token of its own rather than a borrowed scrim, with the label on interactive/ghost/foreground/default.
The background is dropped entirely and the label moves to foreground/disabled.
There is no focus variant. Keyboard focus has to be rendered by the implementation.

rows.Description: Figma stores no timing and no transition is modelled. Every state change is colour or opacity only, with no movement, scale or elevation.
The caret has its own open and closed states, but this component does not drive them. Whatever expands the row is responsible for turning the caret with it.
The badge sits inside the row's layout rather than floating over it, so turning it on takes width away from the label.
The row's name. Fixed row width with no truncation and no wrapping, so length has to be controlled by the writing.

Pinned to Size=small with Framed off and left exposed, so the glyph can be swapped per instance while the sizing stays consistent. See the Icon Metadata frame. It arrives holding Verified, a placeholder rather than a real destination glyph.

Pinned to Size=medium, which is the counter rather than the bare dot, and left exposed so its value stays editable. This is a different size from the one the rail item pins, so the two badges are not interchangeable.
Pinned to the horizontal direction and the closed position, and left exposed so the open state is reachable. Toggled as a whole by Sub Menu.

sections.title: Anatomy
rawTextContent: The outer frame. Fills the width of the slot it sits in and holds a minimum height, so rows in a list line up whatever they contain.
The leading glyph and the label, kept together so the label starts at the same place on every row that has an icon.
A notification indicator between the label and the caret. It sits inside the layout, so it takes width rather than overhanging.
The caret marking a row that opens a further level. Toggled as a whole by the Sub Menu property.

sections.title: How to use
dos: Turn Sub Menu off for rows that navigate straight to a destination. The caret is a promise that another level exists.
Keep the leading icon on for every row in a list, or off for all of them. Mixing the two breaks the label alignment down the panel.
donts: Don't nest more than one level. Only a single indent step is built, so a deeper tree will read as though everything sits at the same depth.
Don't treat this badge as interchangeable with the rail item's. This one is the counter size and sits in the layout, that one is a bare dot that floats over the glyph.

sections.title: Accessibility & Content Guidelines
items: Nesting is conveyed by indent, a quieter label token and a smaller type style, with no connector line. The hierarchy has to be expressed in code as well.
Selection is the only state with a background of its own. Hover and press borrow a translucent scrim and leave the label alone, so neither reaches a keyboard or screen reader user.
There is no focus variant. Keyboard focus has to be rendered by the implementation.
Disabled is visual only and nothing on the row explains why it is unavailable.
The caret marks a row that opens another level but does not describe what is inside it, so the label has to carry that on its own.
Nested rows drop to a 12px type style, which is small for a navigation target. Check it against your minimum readable size.

rows.Description: Fills the slot it sits in, drawn at 184px. It does not hug its label, so rows in a list are all the same width.
48px, held up by a control/lg minimum so the target never drops below it.
4px (space/xs) top and bottom throughout. 12px (space/md) left and right unnested, with the left edge stepping to 24px when nested.
8px (space/sm) between the icon, the label, the badge and the caret.
radius/sm on every variant.
Both 16px, the icon an Icon at Size=small and the caret a Caret Indicator in its horizontal direction.
A 16px Notification Indicator at Size=medium, sitting between the label and the caret rather than overhanging the row.
label/medium (14/20, Medium) unnested, indicator/medium (12/14, Medium) nested.

foreground/primary at rest, foreground/secondary when nested, interactive/ghost/foreground/default when selected, interactive/neutral/foreground/default when pressed and foreground/disabled when disabled. Backgrounds come from the interactive/ghost family.
